messages:
incident-bot: :warning: ALERT: Cluster alert - sustained kubelet OOM restarts on nodes tagged = gpu-infer-us-east. Multiple pods in namespace=redwood-prod terminated. See https://internal.monitoring/alerts/17712

maya_oncall: i'm on it. first glance shows a burst of pod restarts ~10:02am and several node NotReady transitions. Any active rollouts?

jacob_sre: no deploys. `kubectl get nodes -l pool=gpu-infer-us-east -o jsonpath='{.items[*].metadata.name}'` -> inference-gpu-1 inference-gpu-4 inference-gpu-9. Logs show kubelet crashloop on 1 and 9.

lina_infra: pulled system logs from inference-gpu-1: kernel invoked oom_killer, then `systemd` killed containerd. snippet:

    Mar 15 10:02:06 inference-gpu-1 kernel: Out of memory: Killed process 4487 (containerd) total-vm: 134217728kB, anon-rss: 10240000kB
    Mar 15 10:02:06 inference-gpu-1 systemd[1]: kubelet.service: Main process exited, code=killed, status=9/KILL

jacob_sre: container logs from a restarted runner show repeated GPU driver reset: `E GPU: cuCtxCreate failed: CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_INSTRUCTION` then memory accounting fails on attempt to allocate 8GB chunk.

tom_support: flagging customer impact: support dashboard shows 27 unique requests returned 5xx in last 15m; two customers marked enterprise reported degraded latency. I've opened support ticket S-17712 and DM'd account owners.

maya_oncall: quick mitigation suggestion: 1) cordon affected nodes to stop new scheduling, 2) increase autoscaler min for gpu-infer pool by +3 nodes, 3) toggle router to route heavy requests to the pre-warmed dedicated cluster in us-west. thoughts?

jacob_sre: +1 to cordon. do NOT drain immediately - draining causes mass pod evictions and makes kubelet churn worse when containerd restarts. Instead delete resident inference containers (they will restart on healthy nodes) and lower per-model memory limits via dynamic config to force fallback to smaller shard sizes.

lina_infra: scaling up now (requested 3 warm gpu instances). also starting remote session on inference-gpu-1 for live debug. attempting `sudo systemctl restart nvidia-persistenced && sudo modprobe -r nvidia && sudo modprobe nvidia` as safe restart path for driver. will only reboot if driver restart doesn't hold.

anika_prod: enabling ephemeral fallback: flip config key `serve.fallback.quantized = true` for the web router canary first (5% traffic) to measure quality impact. also adding temporary limit: `max_tokens_per_request=1024`.

deploy-bot: deploy event: rollout id r-17712-fallback started by anika_prod -> canary 5% at 10:08, status: success.

maya_oncall: update +6m: new nodes came up, autoscaler reports them Ready, router accepted capacity. error rate dropped from 14% to 4%, but one node still flapping (inference-gpu-9). lina, status on reimage?

lina_infra: attempted driver reload on gpu-9, but kernel OOM persists after reload. ordering reimage + kernel update for the host. cordoned gpu-9 and placed on remediation queue. keeping gpu-1 cordoned until we validate the runtime.

jacob_sre: digging into model-runner traces: one model (large-chat-xl) shows steady growth in native heap across sessions indicating a leak during attention cache eviction. I pushed a throttling patch to limit concurrent shards per pod: pr/runner-17712-throttle. If accepted, will roll to staging then canary.

tom_support: customer update: posted to affected accounts with ETA ~30m for full stabilization, included workaround (retry with smaller batch sizes). no escalations yet.

maya_oncall: immediate follow-ups: - add cgroup memory.limit_in_bytes for model runner pods; - add host probe to cordon on 3 kubelet restarts within 5m; - schedule post-incident RCA. Assigning jacob to runner fix, lina to infra remediation, anika to routing/fallback verification, tom to customer comms.

anika_prod: monitoring canary quality metrics: no obvious regression at 5% quantized fallback. if stable in 20m, ramp to 30% to relieve load.

deploy-bot: alert: escalation initiated to oncall-lead due to sustained degraded errors >5% for 12m.

maya_oncall: handing off in 12m to night shift. will stay on for another 10 minutes to confirm reimages finish. please post final status in #incident-17712 and update the incident tracker.

lina_infra: reimage finished for inference-gpu-9, node back Ready but kept cordoned pending verification. kernel updated to 5.15.76, nvidia-driver 535.86. quick smoke: `nvidia-smi` stable, no resets in 3m. uncordon planned after 30m validation.

jacob_sre: merged throttle PR and added a metric exporter for per-shard RSS. creating follow-up ticket INF-17712 with remediation list: per-pod cgroup limits, graceful eviction policy, canary of shard-throttling, and test harness for driver-reset simulation.

tom_support: updated customers: status moved to "stabilized"; included postmortem ETA + expected follow-up.

maya_oncall: final update: errors down to baseline, quantized fallback disabled for canary, nodes stable. handing to overnight lead jacob_sre for RCA and action items. closing thread for now; will reopen if recurrence. :white_check_mark:
